final_message:
I reproduced the bug. It is a nil pointer dereference when many `Command`s run in parallel in one process, and it fails on every run I tried. I have not fixed anything.

**Reproduction.** I added one test file, `help_flag_parallel_test.go`, in the repo root. It mirrors the report: a bare `&Command{Name, Usage, Action}` with no `HideHelp` set, run from 64 parallel subtests via `cmd.Run(ctx, nil)`, with a `recover()` that fails the test and prints the stack.

Command, from the repo root:

`go test -run Test_HelpFlagParallelRun -count 5000 -failfast .`

It panicked on 8 of 8 runs, usually within 1 to 13 seconds. With only 8 parallel subtests it was flaky: it failed once, then passed three runs of 20000 iterations each. The machine has 4 cores, so more goroutines made the race much more likely.

Failure output:

```
unexpected panic - 'runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference'
  (*boolValue).Get                flag_bool.go:71
  (*FlagBase[...]).Get            flag_impl.go:192
  (*Command).Value                command.go:533
  (*Command).Bool                 flag_bool.go:28
  (*Command).checkHelp            command.go:186
  (*Command).run                  command_run.go:198
  (*Command).Run                  command_run.go:94
```

Some runs show the panic directly in `FlagBase.Get` at `flag_impl.go:192` instead of inside `boolValue.Get`.

**Likely cause, for you to confirm.** `ensureHelp()` in `command_setup.go` (around lines 203-211) appends the package-level `HelpFlag` to every command and, in the "TODO need to remove hack" block, resets its fields (`applied`, `hasBeenSet`, `Value`, `value = nil`). Every `Run()` goes through this, so parallel runs share and mutate that one flag object. One goroutine's reset (`hf.value = nil`) can land between another goroutine's setup and its `checkHelp()` call, so `Get()` reads a nil `value`.

I confirmed the race with `go test -race -run Test_HelpFlagParallelRun -count 200 -failfast .`. It reports a DATA RACE between two goroutines both writing at `command_setup.go:205`, called from `setupDefaults` at line 79.

The only change in the working tree is the new, untracked `help_flag_parallel_test.go`. The command is saved in `out/run_command.txt`.
patch:
diff --git a/help_flag_parallel_test.go b/help_flag_parallel_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1110cd5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/help_flag_parallel_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"runtime/debug"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// runBareCommand mirrors RunCli from the bug report: a minimal command with
+// no explicit HelpFlag configuration, so Run() goes through ensureHelp() and
+// mutates the package-level HelpFlag.
+func runBareCommand(args []string) {
+	cmd := &Command{
+		Name:  "debug",
+		Usage: "make an explosive entrance",
+		Action: func(_ context.Context, cmd *Command) error {
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+
+	if err := cmd.Run(context.Background(), args); err != nil {
+		fmt.Printf("%s\n", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// Test_HelpFlagParallelRun runs the same bare command from many parallel
+// subtests. Each Run() call resets fields on the shared global HelpFlag in
+// ensureHelp(), which races with other goroutines using it and can nil-deref.
+func Test_HelpFlagParallelRun(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
+		name := fmt.Sprintf("hello_%d", i)
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+
+			defer func() {
+				if r := recover(); r != nil {
+					t.Errorf("unexpected panic - '%v'\n%s", r, debug.Stack())
+				}
+			}()
+
+			runBareCommand(nil)
+		})
+	}
+}
